categories.label: Blade Finance
categories.description: Informal moneylenders (kandhu vatti / meter vatti) charging 2-10% interest per day or per week, collected daily by agents. Common among street vendors, daily-wage workers and small traders.
categories.description_ta: தினசரி அல்லது வாராந்திர அதிக வட்டி வசூலிக்கும் முறைசாரா கடன் கொடுப்பவர்கள் (கந்து வட்டி, மீட்டர் வட்டி). தெருவோர வியாபாரிகள், தினக்கூலி தொழிலாளர்கள் அதிகம் பாதிக்கப்படுகிறார்கள்.
categories.legal_status: Charging exorbitant interest is a criminal offence under the TN Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2003. Unlicensed money lending is illegal under the TN Money Lenders Act, 1957.
first_steps: Stop paying cash without a receipt — keep a written record of every payment.
File a police complaint under the TN Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2003 (call 100/112 if threatened).
Get free legal help from your District Legal Services Authority (call 15100).
Move the balance to a low-interest SHG or MUDRA loan.
first_steps_ta: ரசீது இல்லாமல் பணம் கொடுக்காதீர்கள் — ஒவ்வொரு கட்டணத்தையும் எழுதி வையுங்கள்.
2003 அதிக வட்டி தடைச் சட்டத்தின் கீழ் காவல் நிலையத்தில் புகார் கொடுங்கள் (மிரட்டினால் 100/112).
மாவட்ட சட்ட உதவி மையத்தில் இலவச உதவி பெறுங்கள் (15100).
குறைந்த வட்டி SHG அல்லது முத்ரா கடனுக்கு மாறுங்கள்.

categories.label: Chit Fund Default
categories.description: Registered or unregistered chit funds collapsing, foremen absconding, or members unable to keep paying instalments after taking the prize amount.
categories.description_ta: சீட்டு நிறுவனம் மூடப்படுதல், நடத்துபவர் ஓடிவிடுதல், அல்லது சீட்டு எடுத்த பின் தவணை கட்ட முடியாமல் போவது.
categories.legal_status: Governed by the Chit Funds Act, 1982 — complaints go to the Registrar of Chits (Registration Department). Unregistered schemes can be reported on RBI's Sachet portal.
first_steps: Collect your passbook, receipts and the chit agreement.
Check whether the chit is registered with the Registrar of Chits.
Report unregistered or fraudulent schemes at sachet.rbi.org.in and to the police (EOW).
If you owe instalments, ask the foreman in writing for a revised schedule.
first_steps_ta: பாஸ்புக், ரசீதுகள், சீட்டு ஒப்பந்தத்தை சேகரியுங்கள்.
சீட்டு பதிவு செய்யப்பட்டதா என சீட்டு பதிவாளரிடம் சரிபாருங்கள்.
மோசடி சீட்டுகளை sachet.rbi.org.in மற்றும் பொருளாதார குற்றப் பிரிவில் புகார் செய்யுங்கள்.
தவணை பாக்கி இருந்தால் எழுத்துமூலம் புதிய அட்டவணை கேளுங்கள்.

categories.label: Gold Loan Overdue
categories.description: Loans against gold jewellery from banks, NBFCs, cooperative societies or pawnbrokers becoming overdue, with the risk of the jewellery being auctioned.
categories.description_ta: வங்கி, NBFC, கூட்டுறவு அல்லது அடகுக் கடையில் நகை அடமானக் கடன் நிலுவையாகி ஏல அபாயம் வருவது.
categories.legal_status: RBI rules require lenders to give the borrower prior notice before auctioning pledged gold, conduct a transparent auction, and refund any surplus. Pawnbrokers in TN must be licensed under the TN Pawnbrokers Act, 1943.
first_steps: Ask the lender for your exact outstanding and the auction date in writing.
Pay at least the interest to renew the loan if possible — renewal stops the auction clock.
If auctioned, you are entitled to any amount above your dues — ask for the auction statement.
Complain to the RBI Ombudsman (cms.rbi.org.in) if a bank/NBFC skipped notice.
first_steps_ta: நிலுவை மற்றும் ஏல தேதியை எழுத்துமூலம் கேளுங்கள்.
முடிந்தால் வட்டியை மட்டும் கட்டி கடனை புதுப்பியுங்கள் — ஏலம் தள்ளிப்போகும்.
ஏலம் நடந்தால் கடனுக்கு மேல் கிடைத்த தொகை உங்களுக்கே — ஏல அறிக்கை கேளுங்கள்.
முன்னறிவிப்பு இல்லாமல் ஏலம் விட்டால் RBI குறைதீர்ப்பாளரிடம் (cms.rbi.org.in) புகார் செய்யுங்கள்.

categories.label: Agricultural Debt
categories.description: Crop loans, input credit and informal debt among farmers — often worsened by monsoon failure, floods, pest attacks or crop price crashes.
categories.description_ta: பருவமழை தோல்வி, வெள்ளம், பூச்சி தாக்குதல் அல்லது விலை வீழ்ச்சியால் விவசாயிகளுக்கு ஏற்படும் பயிர்க் கடன் மற்றும் முறைசாரா கடன்.
categories.legal_status: Crop loans via Kisan Credit Card get interest subvention; crop insurance under PMFBY; cooperative crop loans have periodically been waived by the TN government.
first_steps: Ask your bank/cooperative for loan restructuring if crop loss was due to a notified calamity.
File crop-loss claims under PMFBY within the deadline (call 14447).
Move informal debt to a Kisan Credit Card (effective ~4% interest with prompt repayment).
Check PM-KISAN status at pmkisan.gov.in.
first_steps_ta: அறிவிக்கப்பட்ட பேரிடர் இழப்பு என்றால் வங்கியில் கடன் மறுசீரமைப்பு கேளுங்கள்.
PMFBY பயிர் காப்பீடு கோரிக்கையை உரிய காலத்தில் பதிவு செய்யுங்கள் (14447).
முறைசாரா கடனை கிசான் கடன் அட்டைக்கு மாற்றுங்கள் (சரியான நேரத்தில் கட்டினால் ~4% வட்டி).
PM-KISAN நிலையை pmkisan.gov.in-ல் பாருங்கள்.

categories.label: Wedding Debt
categories.description: Debt for weddings — dowry pressure, hall bookings, catering and jewellery — often borrowed from several lenders at once.
categories.description_ta: திருமண செலவுகளுக்காக — வரதட்சணை, மண்டபம், சமையல், நகை — பலரிடம் ஒரே நேரத்தில் கடன் வாங்குவது.
categories.legal_status: Giving or taking dowry is an offence under the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961. Dowry harassment can be reported to the police or the women's helpline 181.
first_steps: List every lender, amount, interest rate and due date in one place.
Repay the highest-interest lender first (avalanche method).
Report any dowry demand — call 181 (women's helpline).
Check TN marriage assistance schemes at your Social Welfare office.
first_steps_ta: ஒவ்வொரு கடன், தொகை, வட்டி, தேதியை ஒரே பட்டியலில் எழுதுங்கள்.
அதிக வட்டி கடனை முதலில் அடையுங்கள்.
வரதட்சணை கேட்டால் 181-ல் புகார் செய்யுங்கள்.
சமூக நலத்துறையில் திருமண உதவித் திட்டங்களை விசாரியுங்கள்.

categories.label: Festival Credit
categories.description: Small informal credit and 'buy now pay later' taken before Pongal, Deepavali or temple festivals for clothes, gifts and celebrations — snowballing year after year.
categories.description_ta: பொங்கல், தீபாவளி, கோயில் திருவிழா செலவுகளுக்கு எடுக்கும் சிறிய கடன்கள் வருடாவருடம் சேர்வது.
categories.legal_status: Usually informal. BNPL and digital credit are covered by RBI's digital lending rules.
first_steps: Start a small monthly recurring deposit (RD) for next year's festival.
Clear the smallest debts first to build momentum (snowball method).
Join an SHG savings group for disciplined saving.
first_steps_ta: அடுத்த பண்டிகைக்கு இப்போதே சிறிய RD தொடங்குங்கள்.
சிறிய கடன்களை முதலில் அடையுங்கள்.
SHG சேமிப்புக் குழுவில் சேருங்கள்.

categories.label: Microfinance (MFI) Over-borrowing
categories.description: Multiple joint-liability group (JLG) loans from microfinance companies with weekly collections — taking one loan to repay another, and group pressure when a member defaults.
categories.description_ta: பல மைக்ரோஃபைனான்ஸ் குழுக் கடன்கள், வாராந்திர வசூல், ஒரு கடனை அடைக்க இன்னொரு கடன், குழு அழுத்தம்.
categories.legal_status: RBI microfinance rules (2022) cap total repayments at 50% of household income and ban coercive recovery. Complaints go to the lender's grievance officer, then the RBI Ombudsman.
first_steps: Add up all weekly EMIs — if they exceed half your household income, the lenders over-lent.
Do not take a new MFI loan to repay an old one.
Report abusive collection agents to the lender's grievance officer and RBI (cms.rbi.org.in).
Ask for a moratorium or longer tenure in writing.
first_steps_ta: எல்லா வார தவணைகளையும் கூட்டுங்கள் — குடும்ப வருமானத்தில் பாதிக்கு மேல் என்றால் அதிகமாக கடன் கொடுத்துள்ளனர்.
பழைய கடனை அடைக்க புதிய MFI கடன் வாங்காதீர்கள்.
மிரட்டும் வசூல் முகவர்களை RBI-ல் (cms.rbi.org.in) புகார் செய்யுங்கள்.
தவணை நீட்டிப்பை எழுத்துமூலம் கேளுங்கள்.

categories.label: Loan App Harassment
categories.description: Instant loan apps that charge hidden fees, access contacts and photos, and harass borrowers or their families with threats and morphed images.
categories.description_ta: மறைமுக கட்டணம் வசூலித்து, தொடர்பு எண்கள், புகைப்படங்களை எடுத்து, மிரட்டும் உடனடி கடன் செயலிகள்.
categories.legal_status: RBI Digital Lending rules require lenders to be RBI-regulated, disclose the full cost (APR) upfront, and forbid accessing contacts or harassment. Threats and morphed images are cyber crimes.
first_steps: Do not pay money under threat — take screenshots of every threat and payment.
Report immediately to the Cyber Crime helpline 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in.
Check if the lender is RBI-registered; report illegal apps at sachet.rbi.org.in.
Revoke the app's contacts/photos permission and uninstall it after saving evidence.
Tell your family and friends in advance that you are being targeted — it removes the app's leverage.
first_steps_ta: மிரட்டலுக்கு பணம் கொடுக்காதீர்கள் — எல்லா மிரட்டல்களையும் ஸ்கிரீன்ஷாட் எடுங்கள்.
உடனே சைபர் குற்ற உதவி எண் 1930 அல்லது cybercrime.gov.in-ல் புகார் செய்யுங்கள்.
செயலி RBI பதிவு பெற்றதா என பாருங்கள்; சட்டவிரோத செயலிகளை sachet.rbi.org.in-ல் புகார் செய்யுங்கள்.
ஆதாரங்களை சேமித்த பின் அனுமதிகளை நீக்கி செயலியை நீக்குங்கள்.
குடும்பத்தினருக்கு முன்கூட்டியே சொல்லுங்கள் — மிரட்டலின் சக்தி குறையும்.

categories.label: Medical Debt
categories.description: Debt from hospital bills, surgery, dialysis, cancer treatment or long-term medicines — often borrowed urgently at high interest.
categories.description_ta: மருத்துவமனை கட்டணம், அறுவை சிகிச்சை, டயாலிசிஸ், புற்றுநோய் சிகிச்சைக்காக அவசரமாக அதிக வட்டியில் வாங்கும் கடன்.
categories.legal_status: CMCHIS / PM-JAY cover up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for listed procedures in empanelled hospitals — cashless.
first_steps: Check eligibility for the CM Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (CMCHIS) — call 1800-425-3993.
Ask the hospital's insurance desk whether the treatment is covered before paying cash.
For future treatment, use government hospitals and empanelled hospitals.
Ask the hospital for an itemised bill and an instalment plan.
first_steps_ta: முதலமைச்சர் விரிவான மருத்துவக் காப்பீட்டுத் திட்டத்திற்கு தகுதி உள்ளதா பாருங்கள் — 1800-425-3993.
பணம் கட்டும் முன் மருத்துவமனை காப்பீட்டு மையத்தில் கேளுங்கள்.
அரசு மற்றும் அங்கீகரிக்கப்பட்ட மருத்துவமனைகளை பயன்படுத்துங்கள்.
விரிவான பில் மற்றும் தவணை வசதி கேளுங்கள்.

categories.label: Education Loan Stress
categories.description: Education loans or private borrowing for college fees, hostel and coaching — with repayment pressure when a job is delayed.
categories.description_ta: கல்லூரிக் கட்டணம், விடுதி, பயிற்சிக்காக வாங்கிய கல்விக் கடன் — வேலை தாமதமானால் திருப்பிச் செலுத்தும் அழுத்தம்.
categories.legal_status: Banks follow the IBA model education loan scheme with a moratorium (course period + 1 year). Central interest-subsidy schemes help lower-income families.
first_steps: Confirm when your moratorium ends and apply for an extension if you are still job-hunting.
Check eligibility for the central interest subsidy (family income below ₹4.5 lakh) and PM-Vidyalaxmi.
Ask the bank to restructure EMIs to match your starting salary.
Never take a private high-interest loan to pay fees — ask the college for instalments.
first_steps_ta: மொரடோரியம் எப்போது முடியும் என உறுதி செய்து, தேவைப்பட்டால் நீட்டிப்பு கேளுங்கள்.
மத்திய வட்டி மானியம் மற்றும் PM-வித்யாலக்ஷ்மி தகுதியை பாருங்கள்.
சம்பளத்திற்கு ஏற்ப EMI மாற்றம் கேளுங்கள்.
கட்டணத்திற்கு அதிக வட்டி தனியார் கடன் வாங்காதீர்கள் — கல்லூரியிடம் தவணை கேளுங்கள்.

categories.label: Credit Card / Personal Loan
categories.description: Revolving credit-card balances and personal loans growing through minimum-due payments, late fees and 36-45% annual card interest.
categories.description_ta: குறைந்தபட்ச தொகை மட்டும் கட்டுவதால் வளரும் கிரெடிட் கார்டு நிலுவை மற்றும் தனிநபர் கடன் (ஆண்டுக்கு 36-45% வட்டி).
categories.legal_status: RBI rules ban recovery agents from calling before 8 am or after 7 pm, threatening, or contacting your relatives. Complaints go to the bank, then the RBI Ombudsman.
first_steps: Stop using the card and pay more than the minimum due.
Ask the bank to convert the balance into a lower-interest EMI plan.
If recovery agents harass you, note the date/time and complain to the bank and the RBI Ombudsman (cms.rbi.org.in).
Check your credit report free once a year from a credit bureau.
first_steps_ta: கார்டை பயன்படுத்துவதை நிறுத்தி, குறைந்தபட்சத்திற்கு மேல் கட்டுங்கள்.
நிலுவையை குறைந்த வட்டி EMI-ஆக மாற்ற வங்கியிடம் கேளுங்கள்.
வசூல் முகவர்கள் தொல்லை செய்தால் தேதி/நேரம் குறித்து RBI குறைதீர்ப்பாளரிடம் புகார் செய்யுங்கள்.
வருடத்திற்கு ஒருமுறை இலவச கிரெடிட் அறிக்கை பெறுங்கள்.

categories.label: General Financial Stress
categories.description: Money worries that don't fit one debt type yet — job loss, low income, rising expenses, rent arrears or not knowing where to start.
categories.description_ta: வேலை இழப்பு, குறைந்த வருமானம், செலவு அதிகரிப்பு, வாடகை பாக்கி — எங்கு தொடங்குவது என்று தெரியாத நிலை.
first_steps: Write down monthly income and all fixed expenses — clarity reduces panic.
Prioritise rent, food, electricity and medicines before unsecured debts.
Check which government schemes you are eligible for with the Scheme Finder.
Register on the TN Private Job Portal / employment exchange if you lost your job.
first_steps_ta: மாத வருமானம் மற்றும் செலவுகளை எழுதுங்கள் — தெளிவு பதற்றத்தை குறைக்கும்.
வாடகை, உணவு, மின்சாரம், மருந்து — இவற்றுக்கு முன்னுரிமை கொடுங்கள்.
திட்ட கண்டுபிடிப்பான் மூலம் தகுதியான அரசு திட்டங்களை பாருங்கள்.
வேலை இழந்தால் வேலைவாய்ப்பு அலுவலகத்தில் பதிவு செய்யுங்கள்.

schemes.name: Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai
schemes.authority: Government of Tamil Nadu
schemes.benefit: ₹1,000 per month to eligible women heads of family
eligibility: Woman head of a family holding a ration card
Land and electricity-usage limits apply; government employees' families excluded
schemes.description: Monthly income support for women-led households, reducing dependency on informal moneylenders.
schemes.description_ta: பெண் குடும்பத் தலைவிகளுக்கு மாதம் ₹1,000 — முறைசாரா கடனை குறைக்க உதவும்.

schemes.name: Mahalir Thittam — SHG Bank Linkage
schemes.name_ta: மகளிர் திட்டம் — சுய உதவிக் குழு வங்கிக் கடன்
schemes.authority: TN Corporation for Development of Women (TNCDW)
schemes.benefit: Collateral-free bank loans for women's Self Help Groups at low interest, with interest subvention for prompt repayment
eligibility: Member of a registered women's SHG
Regular group savings and meetings for about 6 months
Group graded by the bank / Mahalir Thittam
schemes.description: The best structural replacement for blade finance: SHG loans cost a fraction of informal interest and build credit history.
schemes.description_ta: கந்து வட்டிக்கு சிறந்த மாற்று — SHG கடன் மிகக் குறைந்த வட்டியில், கடன் வரலாற்றையும் உருவாக்கும்.

schemes.name: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) — Free Legal Aid
schemes.name_ta: மாவட்ட சட்டப் பணிகள் ஆணைக்குழு — இலவச சட்ட உதவி
schemes.authority: Tamil Nadu State Legal Services Authority (TNSLSA)
schemes.benefit: Free lawyer, free court filings, free legal advice and Lok Adalat settlements
eligibility: Victims of disaster, violence or exploitation; industrial workers
Others below the notified income limit
schemes.description: Free legal representation to fight illegal moneylenders, harassment and unfair recovery — and Lok Adalat to settle bank dues with waivers.
schemes.description_ta: சட்டவிரோத கடன் கொடுப்பவர்கள், மிரட்டல்களுக்கு எதிராக இலவச வழக்கறிஞர் — லோக் அதாலத் மூலம் கடன் தீர்வு.

schemes.name: RBI Integrated Ombudsman (CMS)
schemes.authority: Reserve Bank of India
schemes.benefit: Free complaint against banks, NBFCs and digital lenders for harassment, wrong charges, or unfair recovery — compensation possible
eligibility: Customer of a bank, NBFC, or RBI-regulated lender
Complain to the lender first; escalate if no reply in 30 days
schemes.description: File complaints against regulated lenders for coercive recovery, hidden charges, or auctions without notice.
schemes.description_ta: வங்கி / NBFC மிரட்டல், மறைமுக கட்டணம், முன்னறிவிப்பு இல்லாத ஏலம் — இலவசமாக புகார் செய்யலாம்.

schemes.name: National Cyber Crime Reporting (1930)
schemes.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs (I4C) / TN Cyber Crime Wing
schemes.benefit: Report loan-app threats, morphed photos, online fraud; quick reporting can freeze fraud transfers
eligibility: Anyone facing online harassment or financial fraud
schemes.description: Immediate reporting for loan-app extortion and online financial fraud.
schemes.description_ta: கடன் செயலி மிரட்டல், மாற்றப்பட்ட புகைப்படங்கள், ஆன்லைன் மோசடி — உடனே புகார் செய்யுங்கள்.

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC) with Interest Subvention
schemes.authority: RBI / NABARD — via banks and cooperatives
schemes.benefit: Short-term crop loans at 7% interest, effectively 4% with prompt repayment (interest subvention on eligible limits)
eligibility: Farmers — owner cultivators, tenant farmers, sharecroppers
schemes.description: Replaces moneylender crop credit with cheap bank credit.
schemes.description_ta: விவசாயிகளுக்கு குறைந்த வட்டி பயிர்க் கடன் — சரியாக கட்டினால் ~4%.

schemes.name: CM Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (CMCHIS) + PM-JAY
schemes.authority: Government of Tamil Nadu (integrated with Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY)
schemes.benefit: Cashless treatment up to ₹5 lakh per family per year in empanelled hospitals
eligibility: Annual family income up to ₹1.2 lakh (certificate from VAO)
Other notified categories (e.g. migrant workers, Sri Lankan Tamil refugees)
schemes.description: Prevents medical debt — use it before borrowing for treatment.
schemes.description_ta: மருத்துவக் கடனைத் தவிர்க்கும் — சிகிச்சைக்கு கடன் வாங்கும் முன் பயன்படுத்துங்கள்.

schemes.name: RBI Sachet — Report Illegal Lenders & Schemes
schemes.authority: Reserve Bank of India (with State Governments)
schemes.benefit: Check whether a lender/scheme is registered and report unauthorised lending apps, deposit and chit schemes
schemes.description: Verify a lender before borrowing and report fraudulent chit or deposit schemes.
schemes.description_ta: கடன் வாங்கும் முன் நிறுவனம் பதிவு பெற்றதா என சரிபாருங்கள்; மோசடி சீட்டுகளை புகார் செய்யுங்கள்.

schemes.name: PM MUDRA Yojana (Shishu / Kishore / Tarun)
schemes.authority: Ministry of Finance — via banks, NBFCs, MFIs
schemes.benefit: Collateral-free business loans: Shishu up to ₹50,000, Kishore up to ₹5 lakh, Tarun up to ₹10 lakh (Tarun Plus up to ₹20 lakh) at bank rates
schemes.description: Formal bank credit for small businesses at a fraction of moneylender interest.
schemes.description_ta: சிறு தொழிலுக்கு பிணையில்லா வங்கிக் கடன் — கந்து வட்டியை விட பல மடங்கு குறைவு.

schemes.name: PM SVANidhi — Street Vendor Loan
schemes.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
schemes.benefit: Collateral-free working-capital loans in increasing tranches, interest subsidy on timely repayment, and digital cashback
eligibility: Vending certificate / ID or recommendation letter from the urban local body
schemes.description: Replaces daily 'meter vatti' for vendors with cheap formal credit and builds a credit history.
schemes.description_ta: தெருவோர வியாபாரிகளுக்கு மீட்டர் வட்டிக்கு பதில் குறைந்த வட்டி கடன்.

schemes.name: PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi
schemes.authority: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
schemes.benefit: ₹6,000 per year in three ₹2,000 instalments to landholding farmer families
eligibility: Farmer family with cultivable land in their name
Not an income-tax payer, government employee or pensioner above limits
schemes.description: Direct income support for farmers.
schemes.description_ta: விவசாயிகளுக்கு ஆண்டுக்கு ₹6,000.

schemes.name: PM Fasal Bima Yojana (Crop Insurance)
schemes.authority: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / TN Agriculture Dept
schemes.benefit: Crop insurance at low premium (2% kharif, 1.5% rabi, 5% commercial crops) against drought, flood, pests
eligibility: All farmers growing notified crops in notified areas
Enrol before the season's cut-off date
schemes.description: Protects farmers from debt spirals after crop failure.
schemes.description_ta: வறட்சி, வெள்ளம், பூச்சியால் பயிர் இழப்புக்கு காப்பீடு.

schemes.name: Pudhumai Penn Scheme
schemes.authority: Government of Tamil Nadu — Social Welfare Dept
schemes.benefit: ₹1,000 per month to girl students in higher education who studied classes 6–12 in government schools
eligibility: Studied classes 6–12 in a TN government (or notified) school
schemes.description: Reduces borrowing for daughters' college expenses.
schemes.description_ta: அரசுப் பள்ளியில் படித்த மாணவிகளுக்கு உயர்கல்வியில் மாதம் ₹1,000.

schemes.name: Tamil Pudhalvan Scheme
schemes.authority: Government of Tamil Nadu
schemes.benefit: ₹1,000 per month to boys in higher education who studied classes 6–12 in government schools
eligibility: Studied classes 6–12 in a TN government school
schemes.description: Reduces borrowing for sons' college expenses.
schemes.description_ta: அரசுப் பள்ளியில் படித்த மாணவர்களுக்கு உயர்கல்வியில் மாதம் ₹1,000.

schemes.name: Central Interest Subsidy on Education Loans (CSIS) & PM-Vidyalaxmi
schemes.authority: Ministry of Education — via banks
schemes.benefit: Interest subsidy during the moratorium for families below ₹4.5 lakh income; PM-Vidyalaxmi offers collateral-free loans for quality institutions with 3% interest subvention for incomes up to ₹8 lakh
eligibility: Education loan under IBA model scheme
schemes.description: Cuts the cost of education loans for lower-income families.
schemes.description_ta: குறைந்த வருமான குடும்பங்களுக்கு கல்விக் கடன் வட்டி மானியம்.

schemes.name: TN Unorganised Workers Welfare Boards
schemes.authority: Government of Tamil Nadu — Labour Welfare Dept
schemes.benefit: Registered workers get education, marriage, maternity, accident and death assistance
eligibility: Unorganised worker age 18–60 (construction, domestic, auto, street vending etc.)
Registration with the relevant welfare board
schemes.description: Registration unlocks marriage and education assistance that prevents wedding and fee debt.
schemes.description_ta: பதிவு செய்தால் திருமணம், கல்வி உதவித்தொகை கிடைக்கும் — கடனை தவிர்க்கலாம்.

schemes.name: Lok Adalat — Settle Loans with Waivers
schemes.authority: NALSA / TNSLSA
schemes.benefit: Banks often offer one-time settlements with interest waivers; the award is final and has no court fee
eligibility: Anyone with a pending or pre-litigation bank/loan dispute
schemes.description: A faster, cheaper way to close an overdue bank loan.
schemes.description_ta: வங்கிக் கடனை வட்டி தள்ளுபடியுடன் விரைவாக முடிக்கும் வழி.

schemes.name: Stand-Up India
schemes.authority: Ministry of Finance / SIDBI
schemes.benefit: Bank loans from ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore for new enterprises
schemes.description: Larger formal credit to start a business — a path out of informal debt.
schemes.description_ta: புதிய தொழில் தொடங்க SC/ST மற்றும் பெண்களுக்கு வங்கிக் கடன்.

schemes.name: NEEDS — New Entrepreneur-cum-Enterprise Development Scheme
schemes.authority: Government of Tamil Nadu — MSME Department
schemes.benefit: Capital subsidy and interest subvention for educated first-generation entrepreneurs
eligibility: Age limits apply (relaxed for special categories)
schemes.description: Subsidised capital to start a business — useful after job loss.
schemes.description_ta: முதல் தலைமுறை தொழில் முனைவோருக்கு மானியம்.

schemes.name: UYEGP — Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme
schemes.authority: Government of Tamil Nadu — MSME Department
schemes.benefit: Bank loan with 25% government subsidy for small manufacturing, service and business ventures
eligibility: Unemployed youth, age 18–45 (relaxed for special categories)
Family income below the notified limit
schemes.description: Self-employment support with subsidy for unemployed youth.
schemes.description_ta: வேலையில்லா இளைஞர்களுக்கு மானியத்துடன் சுயதொழில் கடன்.

schemes.name: PMEGP — Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
schemes.authority: Ministry of MSME / KVIC
schemes.benefit: 15–35% margin-money subsidy on project cost for new micro-enterprises
schemes.description: Subsidy-backed loans to start micro-enterprises in rural and urban areas.
schemes.description_ta: புதிய சிறு தொழில்களுக்கு 15–35% மானியம்.

schemes.name: PM Jan Dhan Yojana
schemes.authority: Ministry of Finance
schemes.benefit: Zero-balance bank account with RuPay card, accident insurance cover and overdraft facility
eligibility: Any Indian resident aged 10+ without a bank account
schemes.description: First step out of cash-only informal lending — needed for DBT schemes.
schemes.description_ta: பூஜ்ய இருப்பு வங்கிக் கணக்கு — அரசு உதவித் தொகை பெற அவசியம்.

schemes.name: PMJJBY & PMSBY — Low-cost Life and Accident Insurance
schemes.name_ta: குறைந்த கட்டண ஆயுள் மற்றும் விபத்துக் காப்பீடு
schemes.authority: Ministry of Finance — via banks
schemes.benefit: ₹2 lakh life cover for ₹436/year (PMJJBY, age 18–50) and ₹2 lakh accident cover for ₹20/year (PMSBY, age 18–70)
schemes.description: Protects the family from debt if the earning member dies or is disabled.
schemes.description_ta: சம்பாதிப்பவருக்கு ஏதாவது ஆனால் குடும்பம் கடனில் சிக்காமல் காக்கும்.

schemes.name: Atal Pension Yojana
schemes.authority: PFRDA — via banks
schemes.benefit: Guaranteed pension of ₹1,000–₹5,000 per month after age 60
schemes.description: Old-age security for unorganised-sector workers.
schemes.description_ta: அமைப்புசாரா தொழிலாளர்களுக்கு முதுமைக் கால ஓய்வூதியம்.

laws.name: Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2003
laws.name_ta: தமிழ்நாடு அதிக வட்டி வசூலிப்பு தடைச் சட்டம், 2003
laws.summary: Makes it a criminal offence to charge interest above the rates notified by the government, or to use force, threats or harassment to recover a loan. Covers kandhu vatti, meter vatti and daily-interest lending.
laws.summary_ta: அரசு நிர்ணயித்ததற்கு மேல் வட்டி வசூலிப்பது, மிரட்டி வசூலிப்பது குற்றம். கந்து வட்டி, மீட்டர் வட்டிக்கு பொருந்தும்.
your_rights: You can file a police complaint against a lender charging exorbitant interest.
Molesting, threatening or forcibly collecting from a borrower is punishable with imprisonment.
Property documents taken as security can be recovered through legal action.
laws.how_to_act: Go to the nearest police station or Superintendent of Police office with your payment records. If police do not register the complaint, approach the DLSA (15100).

laws.name: Tamil Nadu Money-Lenders Act, 1957
laws.summary: Money lenders must be licensed, keep accounts and give borrowers receipts and statements. Unlicensed lenders face penalties.
laws.summary_ta: கடன் கொடுப்பவர்கள் உரிமம் பெற வேண்டும், கணக்கு வைக்க வேண்டும், ரசீது தர வேண்டும்.
your_rights: Ask for a receipt for every payment.
Ask for a statement of account.
An unlicensed lender's recovery can be challenged.
laws.how_to_act: Ask the lender for their licence number and receipts. Report unlicensed lending to the police and the Revenue/Tahsildar office.

laws.name: Tamil Nadu Pawnbrokers Act, 1943
laws.summary: Pawnbrokers must be licensed, issue a pawn ticket, follow notified interest limits and give notice before selling unredeemed pledges.
laws.summary_ta: அடகுக் கடைக்கு உரிமம் தேவை, அடகுச் சீட்டு தர வேண்டும், விற்கும் முன் அறிவிப்பு தர வேண்டும்.
your_rights: Get a pawn ticket with the item description and interest rate.
Receive notice before your pledge is sold.
Receive any surplus after the sale.
laws.how_to_act: Keep your pawn ticket safe. Complain to the Tahsildar / police if the broker refuses notice or surplus.

laws.name: RBI rules on gold loans (banks & NBFCs)
laws.summary: Regulated lenders must disclose terms, give the borrower prior notice before auction, auction transparently and return any surplus. RBI's 2025 directions also standardise loan-to-value limits and require pledged gold to be returned promptly after repayment.
laws.summary_ta: ஏலத்திற்கு முன் அறிவிப்பு, வெளிப்படையான ஏலம், மீதித் தொகை திருப்பித் தருதல் கட்டாயம். கடன் அடைத்தவுடன் நகையை உடனே திருப்பித் தர வேண்டும்.
your_rights: Prior notice before auction.
Surplus from the auction belongs to you.
Your gold must be returned promptly after full repayment.
laws.how_to_act: Complain to the lender's grievance officer; if unresolved in 30 days, file at cms.rbi.org.in (14448).

laws.name: Chit Funds Act, 1982
laws.summary: Chit funds must be registered with the Registrar of Chits; the foreman must keep security, follow the bye-laws and pay the prize amount on time.
laws.summary_ta: சீட்டு நிறுவனங்கள் பதிவு செய்யப்பட வேண்டும்; நடத்துபவர் பாதுகாப்புத் தொகை வைக்க வேண்டும்.
your_rights: Inspect chit records.
Raise a dispute with the Registrar of Chits.
Running an unregistered chit is an offence.
laws.how_to_act: File a complaint with the District Registrar (Chits) in the Registration Department; for fraud, approach the Economic Offences Wing.

laws.name: Banning of Unregulated Deposit Schemes Act, 2019
laws.summary: Bans taking deposits through unregulated schemes; allows attachment of the operator's property to repay depositors.
laws.summary_ta: அனுமதி இல்லாத வைப்புத் திட்டங்கள் தடை; நடத்துபவரின் சொத்தை முடக்கி பணம் திருப்பித் தரலாம்.
your_rights: Report the scheme to the police/EOW.
Claim from attached properties through the competent authority.
laws.how_to_act: Report at sachet.rbi.org.in and to the TN Economic Offences Wing.

laws.name: RBI Digital Lending Rules (2022 guidelines / 2025 directions)
laws.summary: Loans must come from an RBI-regulated entity; the full cost (annual percentage rate) must be shown upfront in a Key Fact Statement; money must go directly to your bank account; apps cannot access your contacts or photos; you get a free-look period to exit.
laws.summary_ta: கடன் RBI பதிவு பெற்ற நிறுவனத்திடமிருந்து மட்டுமே; முழு செலவு முன்கூட்டியே காட்ட வேண்டும்; தொடர்பு எண்கள், புகைப்படங்களை எடுக்கக் கூடாது.
your_rights: A Key Fact Statement with the APR before you sign.
No access to your contacts, photos or media.
A cooling-off period to repay principal and exit without penalty.
A named grievance officer who must respond.
laws.how_to_act: Report threats to 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in; report illegal apps at sachet.rbi.org.in; complain about regulated lenders at cms.rbi.org.in.

laws.name: IT Act, 2000 and BNS provisions on extortion, intimidation and defamation
laws.summary: Sending obscene or morphed images, threatening messages and extortion are criminal offences.
laws.summary_ta: மாற்றப்பட்ட புகைப்படங்கள், மிரட்டல் செய்திகள், பணம் பறித்தல் — குற்றச் செயல்கள்.
your_rights: Police must register a complaint of cyber harassment.
Platforms must remove such content on complaint.
laws.how_to_act: Call 1930 or file at cybercrime.gov.in with screenshots; visit the district cyber crime police station.

laws.name: RBI Microfinance Regulations, 2022
laws.summary: Total loan repayments of a household (all lenders) must not exceed 50% of household income; lenders must assess income, disclose pricing, and must not use coercive recovery.
laws.summary_ta: எல்லா கடன்களின் தவணையும் குடும்ப வருமானத்தில் 50%-ஐ மீறக் கூடாது; மிரட்டி வசூலிக்கக் கூடாது.
your_rights: Repayment cap of 50% of household income.
No abusive language, late-night visits or public shaming.
A clear factsheet with the interest rate.
laws.how_to_act: Complain to the MFI grievance officer, then cms.rbi.org.in (14448).

q: How do I make a monthly budget?
faq.a:
Start with **one month of real numbers**:
1. Write your take-home income (all earners).
2. List fixed costs first: rent, food, power, school fees, medicines, transport.
3. Add every loan payment (EMIs, weekly vatti, chit instalments).
4. Whatever is left is for savings and other spending.

A simple target: **essentials ≤ 50–60%, loan repayments ≤ 30%, savings ≥ 10%**. If loans take more than 40% of income, that's a debt-trap warning — talk to your lenders about longer tenure before you miss payments. The **Budget Planner** in Tools does this math for you.

q: how much should I save for emergencies
faq.a:
An emergency fund is money kept aside only for shocks — illness, job loss, a broken two-wheeler — so you don't have to borrow from a moneylender.

- **Goal:** 3 months of essential expenses (start with ₹5,000–₹10,000 as a first milestone).
- **Where:** a savings account or a recurring deposit you can break, *not* in a chit or gold you'd have to pawn.
- **How:** set an automatic transfer on salary day, even ₹500 a month. Build it in parallel with repaying high-interest debt.

q: How can I save money on a low income?
salary is small how to save
faq.a:
Small, automatic steps work better than big plans:
1. **Pay yourself first** — move ₹200–₹500 to a separate account or RD on payday.
2. **Use what you're entitled to** — ration card PDS, KMUT ₹1,000/month for eligible women heads, free bus travel for women in TN town buses, scholarships.
3. **Join an SHG** — regular group savings plus cheap credit.
4. **Cut the costliest leak first** — usually high-interest daily/weekly loans.
5. **Track cash for one month** — small daily spends (tea, snacks, recharges) add up.

Open the **Scheme Finder** to see benefits you may be missing.

q: Should I put money in RD or FD?
faq.a:
- **Recurring Deposit (RD):** you deposit a fixed amount every month (e.g. ₹500) for 1–5 years and earn interest. Great for building a festival or emergency fund.
- **Fixed Deposit (FD):** one lump sum locked for a period. Good once you already have savings.

Bank and post-office deposits are regulated and insured (bank deposits up to ₹5 lakh per bank under DICGC). They pay less than chit funds promise, but you won't lose your money if an organiser runs away. Rates change — check your bank or post office.

q: What post office savings schemes are there?
faq.a:
India Post small-savings schemes are government-backed:
- **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana** — for a girl child under 10; long-term savings for her education/marriage, tax benefits.
- **PPF** — 15-year account, tax-free returns, small yearly minimum.
- **Post Office RD / Time Deposit / Monthly Income Scheme (MIS)** — safe regular savings or monthly interest.
- **Senior Citizens Savings Scheme** — for 60+.

Interest rates are revised every quarter — ask your nearest post office or check indiapost.gov.in.

q: how to check if a chit is registered
faq.a:
Chit funds are legal **only if registered** under the Chit Funds Act, 1982 with the Registrar of Chits (TN Registration Department).

Before joining:
1. Ask for the **registration number** and verify it with the District Registrar.
2. Get a written agreement and receipts for every instalment.
3. Be wary of very high promised returns or 'only cash' collection.

Informal neighbourhood chits have no protection if the organiser absconds. A bank RD is safer for savings; an SHG loan is cheaper for borrowing. Report fraud at sachet.rbi.org.in or to the police Economic Offences Wing.

q: How do I open a bank account with no money?
faq.a:
You can open a **zero-balance account (PMJDY / BSBD)** at any bank branch or Bank Mitra with Aadhaar (or other ID and address proof). It comes with a RuPay card and is needed to receive government benefits like KMUT and PM-KISAN directly.

Tips: link your mobile number, never share your OTP/PIN, and ask the bank to enable UPI so you don't have to carry cash. Helpline: 1800-11-0001.

q: Money was taken from my account by fraud
faq.a:
**Act within the first hour — speed matters:**
1. Call **1930** (National Cyber Crime Helpline) or file at **cybercrime.gov.in** — they can freeze the money in transit.
2. Call your bank's customer care (number on the back of your card / official app) and **block your card/UPI**.
3. Give the bank a written complaint. Under RBI rules, if a fraud wasn't your fault and you report it within **3 working days**, your liability can be **zero**.
4. Keep screenshots, the transaction ID and the fraudster's number.

Never pay anyone who calls promising to 'recover' your money — that is a second scam.

q: Someone is asking for my OTP
faq.a:
**Banks, RBI, police and government never ask for your OTP, PIN, CVV or to install a screen-sharing app.** Common traps:
- 'Your KYC expired / account will be blocked — click this link'
- 'You won a prize / refund — enter your UPI PIN to receive' (a PIN is only for *sending* money)
- Fake customer-care numbers from search results
- 'Courier/drugs found in your name — digital arrest' video calls

Hang up, don't click, and verify using the number printed on your card or passbook. Report suspicious numbers on the **Sanchar Saathi** portal (Chakshu) and frauds on **1930**.

q: Police called saying I am under digital arrest
faq.a: **'Digital arrest' is a scam. Real police never arrest anyone over a video call or ask you to transfer money to 'verify' your account.** Disconnect immediately, don't stay on camera, and don't send money. Tell a family member, then report on **1930** / cybercrime.gov.in. If you already paid, report within the hour so the transfer can be frozen.

A bounced cheque can lead to a case under **Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act**:
- The payee must send you a legal notice within 30 days of the bounce.
- You then have **15 days** to pay before they can file a complaint.

If a moneylender is misusing a **blank/security cheque** you gave years ago for a loan you've already repaid (or for illegal interest), don't ignore notices — keep your repayment proof and contact free legal aid (**DLSA 15100**). Courts examine whether a legally enforceable debt actually exists.

q: how to check my credit score free
faq.a:
A **credit score** (300–900; CIBIL is one bureau) shows lenders how reliably you repay. Around **750+** gets better loan offers.

You can get a **free full credit report once a year from each bureau** — CIBIL, Experian, Equifax and CRIF High Mark — on their websites. Check it for loans you never took (a sign of identity fraud) and dispute errors with the bureau.

Informal loans (moneylenders, chits) don't appear in it — which is also why an SHG/MUDRA loan repaid on time helps you *build* a score.

q: How can I improve my credit score?
faq.a:
1. **Pay every EMI and card bill on time** — set auto-debit for at least the minimum.
2. **Keep credit-card use under ~30% of the limit.**
3. **Don't apply for many loans at once** — each application is a hard enquiry.
4. **Avoid 'settlement'** if you can repay — 'settled' stays on your report for years; 'closed' is better.
5. Keep old cards/accounts open if they have a good record.
6. Dispute any wrong entry with the bureau.

Scores usually recover within 6–12 months of consistent on-time payments.

A **one-time settlement (OTS)** lets you pay less than you owe and close the dispute — useful when you truly can't repay in full.

Before you agree:
- Get the offer **in writing on bank letterhead**, with the exact amount and deadline.
- Pay only to the bank's official account — never cash to an agent.
- Collect a **No Dues Certificate** afterwards.
- Know that your credit report will show 'settled', which lowers your score for a few years.

Lok Adalats (free, via DLSA 15100) often help negotiate settlements with interest waivers.

q: Can I close my loan early?
faq.a:
Usually yes, and it saves interest. Under RBI rules, banks and NBFCs **can't charge foreclosure/prepayment penalties on floating-rate loans to individuals** (non-business). Fixed-rate loans may carry a small charge — check your loan agreement.

Prepay the **highest-interest debt first** (moneylender → credit card → personal loan → gold/home loan). After closing, collect the No Dues Certificate and, for gold loans, your jewellery the same day.

q: why is my loan interest so high
faq.a:
- **Flat rate:** interest is charged on the *original* amount for the whole loan, even as you repay — so '12% flat' really costs about **22% a year**.
- **Reducing balance:** interest only on what you still owe — the honest comparison.

Always ask for the **APR (annual percentage rate)** including processing fees. RBI requires regulated lenders to give a **Key Fact Statement** showing it. Use the **True Interest Rate** tool to convert daily/weekly/monthly rates.

q: I have many loans, how do I manage?
should I take one loan to close all loans
faq.a:
1. **List every debt**: lender, balance, interest rate, minimum payment.
2. **Never borrow from a new informal lender to repay an old one** — that's how traps deepen.
3. A **consolidation loan helps only if its rate is lower** (e.g. replacing a 120%/yr moneylender loan with a 10–12% SHG/MUDRA/gold loan from a bank).
4. Pay minimums on everything, put every extra rupee on the **highest-interest** debt (avalanche) or the **smallest** one for quick wins (snowball).

The **Debt Payoff Planner** in Tools compares both and shows your debt-free date.

q: I can't pay my EMI this month
faq.a:
**Talk to the lender *before* the due date** — silence is what escalates things.
1. Write to the branch/grievance officer explaining the reason (job loss, illness) and ask for a **restructure, longer tenure or short moratorium**.
2. Pay whatever partial amount you can and keep receipts.
3. A missed EMI brings a late fee and a credit-score hit; after **90 days** the loan becomes an NPA and recovery starts.
4. Recovery agents must follow RBI rules (calls only **8 am–7 pm**, no threats, no shaming).

Prioritise rent, food and medicine first, then the highest-interest/secured loans.

q: bank agent came home and shouted
Can the bank take my house?
faq.a:
For a **secured loan** (house/property mortgaged), a bank can act under the **SARFAESI Act** after the loan becomes an NPA — but it must first send a **60-day demand notice**. You can reply with objections, and the bank must respond. Agricultural land is excluded from SARFAESI.

An **unsecured** lender (card, personal loan, moneylender) **cannot take your house** without a court order. A private moneylender keeping your property documents or forcing a sale deed is illegal — complain to the police and get free legal aid (**15100**).

q: Moneylender is keeping my house papers
faq.a:
A private lender has no right to hold your **property documents, ration card, ATM card or passbook** as pressure, or to make you sign a sale deed/blank papers.

1. Write down what was taken and when; keep any repayment proof.
2. File a complaint at the police station (or with the SP) under the **TN Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2003**.
3. Contact **DLSA (15100)** for a free lawyer to recover the documents.
4. If an ATM card was taken, **block it with your bank immediately**.

q: Police are not taking my complaint
how to file a police complaint
faq.a:
1. Give a **written complaint** and insist on a receipt (CSR number). You can also file online on the **TN Police citizen portal (eservices.tnpolice.gov.in)**.
2. If the station refuses, send the complaint by **registered post to the Superintendent/Commissioner of Police**.
3. If still no action, a **Judicial Magistrate** can direct the police to register a case — free legal aid (**DLSA 15100**) can help you file it.

For cyber/loan-app harassment you can file directly on **cybercrime.gov.in** or call **1930**.

q: how to settle bank loan in Lok Adalat
faq.a:
**Lok Adalat** is a free, quick settlement forum run by Legal Services Authorities. Banks bring overdue loans there and often agree to **reduced amounts and interest waivers**. There's no court fee, no lawyer needed, and the settlement is final.

National Lok Adalats happen several times a year; you can also ask the **District Legal Services Authority (15100)** to list your case. Bring your loan papers and ID.

q: How do I know if a loan app is genuine?
faq.a:
Before borrowing from any app:
1. Find the **lending bank/NBFC's name** in the app — it must be a regulated entity. Search it on the **RBI website's NBFC list** or **sachet.rbi.org.in**.
2. You must get a **Key Fact Statement** with the APR before signing.
3. Money must come **directly to your bank account** from the lender.
4. Red flags: asks for access to **contacts/photos**, 7-day tenures, huge 'processing fees' deducted upfront, no physical address, WhatsApp-only support.

If in doubt, borrow from a bank, SHG or MUDRA instead.

q: Loan app is sending my morphed photos
app threatening to call my family
faq.a:
This is **extortion — a crime**, and it's not your fault.
1. **Don't pay** under threat; payments only lead to more demands.
2. Take screenshots of every message, number and payment.
3. Report on **1930 / cybercrime.gov.in** and at your district cyber crime police station.
4. Warn family/friends in advance: 'Ignore any messages about me from loan apps.' This removes their leverage.
5. Revoke the app's permissions, then uninstall.
6. Report the app on **sachet.rbi.org.in** and on Google Play.

If the threats are affecting your mental health, call **Tele-MANAS 14416**.

q: How do I apply for Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai?
faq.a:
**Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thogai** gives **₹1,000 a month** to eligible women heads of families in Tamil Nadu.

Broad eligibility: woman head of family on the ration card, age 21+, family income below ₹2.5 lakh a year, with land/electricity-use limits and exclusions for government-employee and income-tax-paying families.

Applications are taken through government camps / ration shops when the window is open, and status can be checked on **kmut.tn.gov.in**. If rejected, you can appeal through the RDO/e-Sevai. Helpline: **1100**.

q: What documents do I need for government schemes?
faq.a:
Keep these ready (and photocopies):
- **Aadhaar** (linked to mobile and bank account)
- **Ration card** (smart card)
- **Bank passbook** (account in your own name, with DBT enabled)
- **Income certificate** and **community certificate** (from VAO/Tahsildar via e-Sevai)
- Address proof, passport photos
- Scheme-specific: land documents (patta/chitta) for farmers, school/college certificates for students, vending certificate for street vendors.

Most certificates can be applied for at a **TN e-Sevai centre** or online at **tnesevai.tn.gov.in**.

q: How do I get an income certificate?
faq.a:
Income, community, residence, first-graduate and other revenue certificates are issued by the Revenue Department via **TN e-Sevai**:
1. Visit an **e-Sevai centre** (taluk office, post offices, many common service centres) or apply at **tnesevai.tn.gov.in**.
2. Bring Aadhaar, ration card, and supporting proof (salary slip / self-declaration for income).
3. The VAO and RI verify, and the Tahsildar approves; you download the e-certificate.

Track your application with the acknowledgement number. Official fees are small — don't pay middlemen.

q: How do I join a self-help group?
faq.a:
**Self-Help Groups** are groups of 10–20 women (also men/mixed in some areas) who save regularly and get **cheap, collateral-free bank loans**.
1. Ask at your **panchayat / ward office, Mahalir Thittam (TNCDW) block office**, or an existing SHG leader nearby.
2. Members save a small fixed amount monthly and keep records.
3. After ~6 months of regular savings the group is graded and linked to a bank for loans, often with **interest subvention** for prompt repayment.

SHG credit is one of the best ways out of kandhu vatti. Mahalir Thittam helpline: 044-24321311.

q: How do I get the CM health insurance card?
faq.a:
**CMCHIS** (integrated with PM-JAY) covers **up to ₹5 lakh per family per year**, cashless, for listed treatments in empanelled government and private hospitals.

- Eligibility: annual family income up to about ₹1.2 lakh (VAO certificate) and other notified groups; senior citizens 70+ are covered under PM-JAY.
- Enrol at the **CMCHIS kiosk in the District Collectorate** or designated centres with your ration card, Aadhaar and income certificate.
- In hospital, go to the **insurance desk first**, before paying.

Helpline: **1800-425-3993** (24×7). Website: cmchistn.com.

1. Ask whether the treatment is covered by **CMCHIS/PM-JAY** or your employer **ESI** — empanelled hospitals must treat covered procedures cashless.
2. Government medical college hospitals provide most treatments free.
3. Ask for an **itemised bill** and question duplicate or unexplained charges.
4. Request an **instalment plan** instead of borrowing at high interest.
5. Hospital/medical social workers and charitable trusts can help with large surgeries.
6. If you have health insurance and the claim is rejected, complain to the insurer, then the **Insurance Ombudsman / Bima Bharosa (IRDAI)**.

1. Ask the insurer for the **rejection reason in writing**.
2. File a complaint with the insurer's **grievance officer**; they must respond within 14 days.
3. If unsatisfied, escalate on **Bima Bharosa (bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in)** or call IRDAI's toll-free number.
4. You can approach the **Insurance Ombudsman** (free, no lawyer needed) for claims up to ₹50 lakh within a year of the final rejection.

Keep the policy document, bills, discharge summary and all correspondence.

Keep insurance and investment separate:
- **Term insurance** gives a large cover (e.g. 10–15× yearly income) for a low premium — best protection for your family if you have dependants and loans.
- Low-cost government options: **PMJJBY** (₹2 lakh life cover, ₹436/year) and **PMSBY** (₹2 lakh accident cover, ₹20/year) through your bank.
- **Health insurance** (or CMCHIS) matters more than savings-type policies.
- Endowment/money-back policies usually give low returns; don't stop an existing one in a panic — check its surrender value first.

q: I lost my job, what should I do?
faq.a:
**First 2 weeks:**
1. Cut to essentials; write to lenders asking for a **moratorium/restructure** before you miss EMIs.
2. If you had **EPF**, you can withdraw **75% after 1 month** of unemployment (the rest after 2 months) via the UAN portal — or keep it if you can manage.
3. Check **ESI unemployment allowance** if you were covered.
4. Register on the **TN Private Job Portal (tnprivatejobs.tn.gov.in)** and employment exchange.
5. Free skilling via **Naan Mudhalvan**; self-employment loans via **UYEGP/NEEDS/PMEGP**.

Avoid 'jobs' that ask you to pay a fee — that's a scam.

q: How can I withdraw my PF?
faq.a:
With an active **UAN** linked to Aadhaar and bank account, you can claim online at the EPFO member portal / UMANG app:
- **Unemployment:** 75% after 1 month, balance after 2 months.
- **Partial advances** for illness, marriage, education, house purchase/repair (rules and limits apply).

Withdrawing early loses compounding for retirement, so treat it as an emergency option — but it's far better than borrowing from a moneylender. EPFO helpline: 14470.

q: Job offer asking me to pay a fee
faq.a:
**Genuine employers don't charge you to get a job.** Common scams: 'like YouTube videos and earn', Telegram 'tasks' that pay small amounts first then ask you to 'invest', overseas jobs with visa fees, government jobs 'through contacts'.

Don't pay, don't share Aadhaar/bank details, and report on **1930 / cybercrime.gov.in**. For overseas jobs, use only agents registered on the **eMigrate** portal.

q: Is this double your money scheme real?
faq.a:
**If someone promises guaranteed high returns (e.g. 'double in a year', '10% a month'), it is almost certainly a Ponzi/MLM fraud.** Early members get paid from new members' money until it collapses — Tamil Nadu has seen many such collapses.

Check whether the company is registered with **SEBI/RBI** (sachet.rbi.org.in). Unregulated deposit schemes are banned under the **BUDS Act, 2019**. Report to the TN **Economic Offences Wing** or sachet.rbi.org.in.

q: I lost money in online rummy
faq.a:
You're not alone — many families in Tamil Nadu have been hurt by online gambling, which is why TN passed the **Prohibition of Online Gambling and Regulation of Online Games Act, 2022**.

1. **Tell one trusted person today** — secrecy feeds the cycle.
2. Block gambling apps/sites, and ask your bank to block gaming merchants.
3. Don't borrow to 'win it back' — chasing losses is the trap.
4. List the debts and make a repayment plan (Debt Payoff Planner).
5. Free, confidential help for urges and stress: **Tele-MANAS 14416**.

Report illegal betting apps to the police / 1930.

q: I am very stressed about money
faq.a:
Money stress is real and heavy — and it's a sign of the pressure you're under, not a personal failing.

Small things that help right now:
- **Write the problem down** (who you owe, how much, by when). Facing the numbers usually feels smaller than carrying them in your head.
- **Take one next step today** — one call, one letter, one form.
- **Talk to someone you trust**; you don't have to solve it alone.
- Breathe slowly (in 4 seconds, out 6) when panic rises; keep some routine and sleep.

If stress becomes unbearable or you have thoughts of harming yourself, please call **Tele-MANAS 14416** (24×7, Tamil) or **112**.

q: How do I tell my family about my debt?
my husband doesn't know about the loan
faq.a:
Hiding debt usually makes it grow. A gentle approach:
1. Pick a calm time and start with how you feel: *'I've been worried and I need your help.'*
2. Share the facts — list of loans, amounts, what led to it — not blame.
3. Bring a plan (even a rough one from the Budget or Payoff planner) so it feels solvable.
4. Agree on one or two changes together.

If you fear violence or abuse when you disclose, prioritise safety — the women's helpline **181** and **112** can help.

q: My husband takes all my salary
family forcing me to take loans
faq.a:
Being forced to hand over earnings, take loans in your name, or bring money from your family is **economic abuse**, recognised under the **Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005**. Dowry demands are illegal.

- Call **181** (women's helpline, 24×7) or **112** in an emergency.
- **One Stop Centres (Sakhi)** in every district offer counselling, legal and police help.
- Free legal aid: **DLSA 15100**.
- Keep a bank account and ID documents that only you control.

q: How do I get a Kisan Credit Card?
faq.a:
Apply at any bank branch or **Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Society (PACCS)** with Aadhaar, land records (patta/chitta/adangal) or a tenancy/lease declaration, and photos.

- Short-term crop loans carry **interest subvention** — around 4% effective for prompt repayment on eligible limits.
- Collateral-free up to the notified limit.
- Also available for **fisheries and animal husbandry**.

Replacing moneylender crop credit with KCC is one of the biggest savings a farmer can make. Kisan Call Centre: **1800-180-1551**.

q: How do I claim crop insurance?
faq.a:
Under **PM Fasal Bima Yojana**:
- **Localised loss** (hailstorm, flood, landslide) or **post-harvest loss**: inform the insurer, bank or agriculture office **within 72 hours** (call **14447** or use the Crop Insurance app).
- Widespread losses are assessed through crop-cutting experiments — you don't need to file separately if you were enrolled.
- Keep your enrolment receipt, land records and photos of damage.

Also ask the bank to **restructure crop loans** when a calamity is notified.

Check **Beneficiary Status** on **pmkisan.gov.in** with your Aadhaar/registration number. Common reasons for a missed instalment:
- **e-KYC not completed** (OTP or biometric at a CSC)
- Aadhaar not seeded / bank account not DBT-enabled
- Land records not verified

Fix these at the agriculture office or a common service centre. Helpline: **155261**.

q: Should I sell gold or take a gold loan?
faq.a:
- **Gold loan from a bank/cooperative** (roughly 9–12% a year) is far cheaper than moneylenders and good for a short, clear need you can repay in months.
- **Pawnbrokers/NBFCs** may charge more — compare the APR.
- If you **can't see how you'll repay**, rolling over the loan and paying interest forever can cost more than the gold is worth; selling part may be wiser.

RBI rules require clear terms, prior notice before auction, and returning any surplus. Never pledge gold to repay another informal loan.

q: I got a gold auction notice
faq.a:
1. Contact the lender **immediately** and ask for the exact dues and auction date in writing.
2. Paying **just the interest** often lets you **renew** the loan and stops the auction.
3. If you can't, ask for time or a part-release (take back some jewels by paying part).
4. If auctioned, you're **entitled to any amount above your dues** — request the auction statement.
5. If a bank/NBFC auctioned without proper notice, complain to the RBI Ombudsman (**cms.rbi.org.in**).

q: When do I start repaying my education loan?
no job but education loan EMI
faq.a:
Under the IBA model scheme, repayment usually starts after a **moratorium of course period + 1 year** (or 6 months after getting a job, whichever is earlier).

If you're still job-hunting: write to the bank requesting an **extension or restructured EMIs**, and check the **Central interest subsidy** (family income below ₹4.5 lakh) for the moratorium period. Pay at least the interest if you can, to stop the balance growing. Lok Adalat (15100) can help with overdue education loans.

q: What scholarships are there for my child?
faq.a:
Look at these before borrowing for fees:
- **Pudhumai Penn / Tamil Pudhalvan** — ₹1,000/month for students from TN government schools in higher education.
- **Post-Matric scholarships** for SC/ST/BC/MBC/minority students (TN Adi Dravidar & Tribal Welfare, BC/MBC departments; **National Scholarship Portal**).
- **First Graduate** fee concession in many TN professional courses.
- **PM-Vidyalaxmi / Vidyalakshmi portal** for education loans with interest subvention.

Ask the college scholarship cell — deadlines matter.

q: Where can I learn a skill for free?
faq.a:
- **Naan Mudhalvan** (naanmudhalvan.tn.gov.in) — TN government skilling platform with free courses and placement support for students and youth.
- **TN Skill Development Corporation** and **PMKVY** short-term courses (electrician, tailoring, nursing assistant, driving, IT, etc.).
- **ITIs and polytechnics** for trade certificates.

Pair a skill with a self-employment loan (UYEGP, PMEGP, MUDRA) if you want to start a small business.

q: I want to start a small business, where can I get a loan?
faq.a:
Collateral-free and subsidised options:
- **PM MUDRA** — Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (up to ₹5 lakh), Tarun (up to ₹10 lakh).
- **PM SVANidhi** — street vendors.
- **UYEGP** (TN) — 25% subsidy for unemployed youth; **NEEDS** (TN) — for educated first-generation entrepreneurs; **PMEGP** — 15–35% subsidy.
- **Stand-Up India** — SC/ST and women entrepreneurs.

Apply with a simple business plan, Aadhaar, bank statements, and quotations. Start small, keep business and home money separate.

q: Is there a scheme to build a house?
faq.a:
- **PMAY-Urban 2.0 / PMAY-Gramin** — central support for building or buying a first house for eligible low-income families (subsidy/interest subsidy, income limits apply).
- **Kalaignar Kanavu Illam** — TN scheme to replace huts with concrete houses in rural areas.
- **TNUHDB (Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board)** tenements for urban poor.

Apply via your local body (panchayat/municipality) or the official portals; never pay 'agents' for allotments.

In Tamil Nadu, the **TN Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act, 2017** governs rentals: tenancies should be written and registered with the Rent Authority, and eviction must follow due process — a landlord **can't cut water/power or throw out belongings** to force you out.

If you're behind on rent: talk early, offer a written repayment schedule, and keep receipts. For disputes, contact the Rent Authority (RDO) or free legal aid (**15100**).

q: How do I get a ration card?
faq.a:
Apply or update (add/remove member, change address) online at **tnpds.gov.in** or via an e-Sevai centre, with Aadhaar of all members and address proof. A ration card gives subsidised rice/sugar/pulses and is needed for many schemes (KMUT, CMCHIS).

Complaints about ration shops: TN PDS helpline **1967** or **1800-425-5901**.

Tamil Nadu's **Social Security Pension schemes** (Revenue Department) provide a monthly pension to destitute elderly, widows, differently-abled persons, deserted wives and unmarried women above notified ages, combined with central NSAP funds.

Apply through the **Tahsildar / e-Sevai** with age proof, Aadhaar, ration card and bank details. For organised-sector retirees, check EPFO pension; for future security, consider **Atal Pension Yojana**. Benefit amounts are revised by government order — confirm at the taluk office.

q: How do I register in the labour welfare board?
faq.a:
TN has **welfare boards for unorganised workers** — construction, domestic, auto/taxi drivers, tailors, street vendors and more. Registered members can get assistance for **children's education, marriage, maternity, accident and death**, and pensions.

Register online at **tnuwwb.tn.gov.in** (or labour office) with Aadhaar, age proof, a work certificate and photos, and **renew on time**. Helpline: 1800-425-2299.

q: Do I need to file income tax?
faq.a:
You must file an ITR if your income is above the basic exemption limit, but **filing even below it can help** — to claim a **TDS refund** (e.g. bank interest or salary TDS), and as income proof for loans/visas.

Under the new tax regime, salaried people with modest incomes often pay **no tax** due to the rebate — check the current limits on **incometax.gov.in**. Filing is free on the official portal; link PAN with Aadhaar first.

q: Is buy now pay later safe?
faq.a:
'Buy now pay later' and 'no-cost EMI' are **loans** — missed payments add late fees and hurt your credit score. 'No-cost' often hides processing fees or lost discounts.

Use them only for planned needs you could pay in cash anyway, keep track of every due date, and avoid stacking several apps — that's how festival-season spending snowballs.

q: I signed as guarantor and now the bank is calling me
faq.a:
As a **guarantor** you are legally liable to repay if the borrower defaults — the bank can recover from you, and it shows on your credit report.

- Ask the bank for the loan statement and talk to the borrower first.
- Negotiate a restructure or settlement jointly.
- If you pay, you can legally recover that amount from the borrower.

In future, guarantee only loans you could afford to repay yourself.

q: Group members are pressuring me to pay
faq.a:
In joint-liability loans, the group shares responsibility — which can turn into painful peer pressure.

- RBI rules say total repayment obligations of a household **shouldn't exceed 50% of household income**; if lenders over-lent, say so in writing.
- Lenders must not use **coercive recovery**, public shaming, or late-night visits.
- Ask the MFI for a **moratorium or rescheduling** for genuine hardship (illness, job loss).
- Complain to the lender's grievance officer, then **cms.rbi.org.in / 14448**.

Don't take a new MFI loan to repay an old one.

q: How do I plan for Deepavali without debt?
faq.a: Divide your expected festival spend by the months left and save that amount monthly in an **RD or a separate account** (a 'festival jar'). Decide a fixed budget for clothes, sweets and gifts **before** shopping, pay in cash/UPI rather than credit, and avoid 'festival offers' on BNPL. If you get a bonus, set part aside for the next festival first.

q: How do I plan a wedding without big loans?
faq.a:
- Agree on a **total budget as a family** before booking anything; social pressure is the biggest cost driver.
- Simple temple or registered marriages and shared community halls cut costs hugely.
- **Dowry is illegal** (Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961) — you can refuse and report demands (181).
- Check **TN marriage assistance schemes** (Social Welfare dept) and welfare-board benefits if you're a registered worker.
- If borrowing, use one formal loan instead of many moneylenders.

q: What interest can a moneylender legally charge?
faq.a:
Private money lending in Tamil Nadu must be **licensed** (TN Money-Lenders Act, 1957), and charging interest above the government-notified rates — or collecting by force — is a **crime under the TN Prohibition of Charging Exorbitant Interest Act, 2003**.

Daily/weekly 'kandhu', 'meter' or 'hourly' vatti (often 120%–3,000%+ a year) falls squarely in that category. Keep payment records and complain to the police; free legal help: **15100**. Use the **True Interest Rate** tool to see the yearly rate you're paying.

q: How do I complain against a bank?
faq.a:
1. Complain to the bank in writing / via its official portal and note the complaint number.
2. If there's no reply in **30 days** or you're unhappy, file with the **RBI Integrated Ombudsman** at **cms.rbi.org.in** (or call **14448**) — free, online, no lawyer needed.
3. Attach statements, letters and screenshots.

The same route covers NBFCs, payment apps and RBI-regulated digital lenders.

q: Bank cut money for minimum balance
faq.a: RBI rules say banks **must not push a savings account into negative balance** due to minimum-balance penalties, and must notify you before levying them. If your income is irregular, ask the bank to convert to a **Basic Savings Bank Deposit (zero-balance) account**. Wrong charges can be disputed with the bank, then the RBI Ombudsman (cms.rbi.org.in).

q: why does my loan keep growing
faq.a:
**Compound interest** means unpaid interest is added to the balance, and next time you pay interest on that bigger amount. With high rates the balance can grow faster than you repay — which is why '10% a week' loans explode.

Example: ₹10,000 at 10% a week, if nothing is paid, becomes about **₹26,000 in 10 weeks**. Paying only interest never reduces the principal. Prioritise paying down high-interest principal, or replace the loan with cheaper credit.
